he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:1.en: The widespread custom throughout Israel is to say Barchu before the Shema is recited. It is not said with fewer than ten, for nothing involving sanctification is said with fewer than ten.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:5.en: Blessed is Adonoy, Who is blessed forever and ever.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:6.en: One must not interrupt at all between Barchu and Yotzer Or, even for a mitzvah (Levush). It is written in the writings that at the beginning of Yotzer Or one must touch the tefillin. Therefore, when saying Yotzer Or, touch the hand tefillin; and at Borei Choshek, touch the head tefillin (Pe'ah).

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:11.en: Holy, holy, holy is Adonoy of Hosts, the fullness of all the earth is His glory.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:13.en: Blessed is the glory of Adonoy from His place.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:15.en: In this blessing are included many things: that the Name loved us more than all nations and gave us the Torah and to believe in His uniqueness and that He is the Master of all. And the Ba'al HaMacharot wrote that they attached Ahavat Olam to Yotzer HaMa'orot because in it He mentions the uniqueness of the Holy One's Name and the giving of the Torah which illuminates more than all the luminaries. For the sun illuminates only by day, but the Torah by day and by night (Avudraham).

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:17.en: And one says Shema Yisrael. And the custom is to say it in a loud voice to arouse the intention in the first verse, which is the main intention. And one should not lengthen the aleph of Echad nor swallow the chet. And one should lengthen the dalet for a measure to make Him King in the four winds of the world (Avudraham). Every place where this circle (°) is written is to indicate to give a pause in every word that begins with the same letter as the end of the preceding word.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:30.en: Anyone who did not say Emet VeYatziv in the morning and Emet VeEmunah in the evening has not fulfilled his obligation, as it is said (Psalms 92:3) 'To declare in the morning Your kindness and Your faithfulness in the nights' (Berachot 12b). And Rashi explains that the blessing of Emet VeYatziv as a whole is on the kindness He did with our fathers, taking them out of Egypt, splitting the sea for them, and passing them through.

he:Weekday Shacharit/The Shema:39.en: The worshipper must have in mind the meaning of the words he utters. If he cannot, he should at least think of things that humble the heart and direct it to his Father in heaven. He should place his feet together as if they were one, pray quietly, not signal with his eyes, lips or fingers, and not interrupt even for Kaddish, Kedushah or Barchu.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Amidah:95.en: When the chazzan reaches "Modim" and bows, the whole congregation bows and says the short thanksgiving that begins likewise with "Modim". It is not the way of a servant to thank his master through an agent; each person must accept the yoke of Heaven in his own mouth, since acceptance through an agent is incomplete and could be denied ("I never sent him").

he:Weekday Shacharit/Tachanun:1.en: On Rosh Chodesh, Chol HaMoed and Chanukah, Hallel is said here after the chazzan's repetition. On public fast days Selichot are said. On days when Tachanun is not said, the chazzan says Half Kaddish.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Tachanun:2.en: A correct reason why the confession was ordained in the plural: one is punished not only for his own sins but also for his fellow's, through mutual responsibility, since all Israel is one body made of many limbs. Therefore one confesses in the plural, to confess for his fellow as well.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Tachanun:11.en: When falling on one's face, some lean to the right (Ps. 16:8), others to the left (Prov. 3:26). Custom: right in Shacharit, left in Mincha.

he:Weekday Shacharit/Avinu Malkeinu:1.en: On public fast days and during the Ten Days of Repentance, Avinu Malkeinu is recited here. Its great merit is recorded in the books. Rabbi Akiva instituted it, corresponding to the middle blessings of the weekday Amidah. Since it contains elements of the eighteen blessings, it is not recited on Shabbat.

Forming, יוצר, is the act of refining or modifying an original substance, whereas, creating, בורא, refers to creating the original substance from nothing. For example, when one shapes a wooden table, to make it round, he “forms” the wood, the original substance which was “created.” Similarly, God “forms the light” which is His act of modifying or limiting the darkness He created.—Siddur HaGra

Making, עושה, is the act of completion, such as when one completes a table by painting it. Similarly, God's finishing touch of creation is “making peace,” the vessel that holds it all together, as stated in the Mishna, “God found no vessel to contain blessing other than peace.” לא מצא הקב״ה כלי מחזיק ברכה אלא השלום—Siddur HaGra

Rabbi Pinchos ben Ya'ir was given two measures of barley for safekeeping. The owner forgot about it for a number of years. Rabbi Pinchos ben Ya'ir planted the barley seed, and each year replanted the previous year's harvest until it grew to be a substantial crop. After seven years, the owner returned to claim his two measures of barley and Rabbi Pinchos told him, “Come I will show you the great fortune you have accumulated.” God does the same with the good and righteous deeds of man.
